        "title": "Continual-ARC task-d7ce8437: match and stamp the marker mask on zeros",
        "content": "Global verified rule for Continual-ARC task-d7ce8437, confirmed by a demonstration and an accepted test. Infer the non-background marker color and the marker's full bounding-box binary mask from the current input; do not hard-code its dimensions or offsets. Scan all in-bounds translations in the same orientation (do not rotate or reflect). A placement matches when every cell at an occupied mask offset is zero; cells at blank mask offsets are don't-care and may contain any value. Recolor the occupied cells of every matching placement to the marker color. Union the recolored cells when matches overlap, and preserve all other cells, including the source marker and nonzero cells at don't-care offsets.",

        "content": "Global verified rule for Continual-ARC task-bbe28dbc. Identify the uniform background, a full straight line of another color (the rail, horizontal or vertical), and a separate contiguous non-background object. Move the whole object, preserving its shape and colors, to the nearest placement adjacent to the rail on the side toward which it can move, preserving its position along the rail. Clear the object's original cells to background. On the moved object's side away from the rail, paint exactly one complete line of color 8 parallel to the rail, one cell beyond the object's far edge. Do not fill the intervening gap. Keep the rail and all other cells unchanged. Verified with a horizontal rail and two-cell object, a vertical rail and 3x9 object, and a solved test with a horizontal rail and two-cell object.",

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Continual-ARC task-43293a65: complete periodic patterns in the indicated orientation",
        "content": "Global verified rule for Continual-ARC task-43293a65, based on four demonstrations and a correctly solved test. Infer the seed pattern's orientation and periodic motif from the nonzero cells, then complete the grid by periodic continuation with the correct phase; preserve known cells. In horizontal-stripe cases, read the seeded rows as a vertical sequence and repeat it cyclically in both directions: [3,9,9,0] completes to [3,9,9,3]; the seed rows [1,9,6] align to the repeating sequence [6,1,9,...]; and the test sequence [0,9,4,0,0] completes to [4,9,4,9,4]. Other examples encode cyclic sequences on diagonal directions, including NW-SE and NE-SW; infer the orientation from the seed and continue periodically along it. Do not assume mirror symmetry: this is periodic completion, not reflection.",

        "title": "Continual-ARC task-1c0718b6: complete selected marker tracks",
        "content": "Global verified rule for Continual-ARC task-1c0718b6, supported by four demonstrations and an accepted test. The grid has a uniform background and sparse markers of another color; add color 2 in gaps along selected coherent horizontal and vertical marker tracks. Infer the selected tracks from each input rather than using a fixed threshold or connecting every pair of collinear markers. Complete vertical tracks first, then horizontal tracks using the vertically added cells; do not recursively propagate horizontal fills back into more columns. The demonstrations show that some lines with only two widely separated markers remain incomplete. In the accepted 19x9 test (background 4, markers 3), add color 2 at row 2 columns 2–3, row 3 column 5, row 4 columns 0–1, row 5 column 0, and row 8 columns 1–2 and 4 (zero-based indexing); leave rows 6–7 between columns 0 and 5 unchanged. Indiscriminate collinear gap-filling and recursive closure that fills a rectangle were both rejected.",

      "continual_arc_task_43293a65_sparse_periodic_stripes": {

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Continual-ARC task-43293a65: infer and complete periodic full-row color sequence",
        "content": "Verified on task-43293a65 with two demos and a correct test. Inputs are grids where each row is a uniform color; zero rows are missing entries and nonzero rows give samples of a vertically periodic color sequence. Infer the shortest positive row period compatible with all observed nonzero rows: for each candidate period p, rows whose indices are congruent mod p must have the same nonzero color. Fill every row from the resulting phase/color mapping, using absolute row index modulo p, and repeat that color across the whole row. Demo 1 had a visible 9-row motif on rows 3-11 which extended above and below; demo 2 had sparse samples consistent with period 8. In the solved test, observed rows 3=4, 5=7, 10=6 force the shortest period p=3, giving phase colors 0->4, 1->6, 2->7; output alternates these full-width rows from row 0 onward. Phase is anchored to absolute row indices, not to the first observed row. Preserve known colors. This rule is for vertically repeating uniform horizontal stripes with zeros as missing rows.",

        "title": "Continual-ARC task-e7a2d445: use the L marker to select a duplicate shape",
        "content": "Global Continual-ARC memory for task-e7a2d445. Across the demonstrations and accepted test, grids contain a mostly uniform background, a large L-shaped marker, and scattered objects that may include matching or duplicated shapes. Recolor the selected matching object to the large marker's color, using the marker's orientation/position to identify the indicated copy; do not choose merely by proximity. The accepted test directly verifies this selection: the large color-7 L marker indicates one of two identical five-cell color-3 shapes. Recolor only the copy at rows 12–13, columns 11–13 (1-based); leave the copy at rows 27–28, columns 14–16 unchanged. Avoid mistaking a nearby small L-shaped object or an unrelated component for the target: those choices were incorrect in earlier attempts. Treat the duplicated-shape selection as directly validated, and do not infer a more specific general selection formula than the examples support.",

        "content": "Global verified rule for Continual-ARC task-fa97545b. The input has two equal-sized panels separated by a single uniform divider column; panel dimensions can vary. Compare aligned cells, treating 0 as empty in both panels regardless of which color is most frequent. Output has the dimensions of either panel: write 2 where both aligned input cells are nonzero, and 0 otherwise. Preserve no other input values in the output. Verified by a 6x25 demonstration (left occupied color 6, right occupied color 3) and an accepted 16x27 test (left occupied color 3, right occupied color 9). Failure avoidance: do not infer empty/background cells by panel color frequency; the right panel may be mostly 3 or 9, but its zero cells are still empty.         "title": "Continual-ARC task-2a787dfa: mark compartments containing exactly two markers",
        "content": "Global verified rule for Continual-ARC task-2a787dfa. The input grid is partitioned by full-width and/or full-height uniform separator lines into an R-by-C array of equal rectangular compartments. Infer the background and sparse marker colors from the compartments, identify separator rows and columns, and count marker cells within each compartment, excluding separators. Output an R-by-C grid: use color 1 for compartments containing exactly two marker cells, and the background color for all other compartments. Do not return the original-sized grid. Verified demo: a 19x11 grid split by separator rows 4, 9, 14 and columns 2, 5, 8 into sixteen 4x2 compartments; only compartment (row 1, column 3) had exactly two markers, and the 4x4 output marked it with 1. Verified test: a 19x5 grid split into four row bands and two columns; the exactly-two-marker compartments produced [[7,7],[7,1],[7,1],[7,7]], accepted as correct. Count carefully and derive compartment dimensions from the separators rather than assuming a fixed layout.",

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Continual-ARC task-cf412e0e: project marker rays and offset-mapped tracks between edge segments",
        "content": "Global verified rule for Continual-ARC task-cf412e0e, supported by four demonstrations and a correctly solved test. A uniform field has two equal-length, same-color edge segments on opposite sides, parallel but shifted along their edges. Interior markers lie on lines perpendicular to one segment. For each marker, extend the marker's original color in a straight ray from the marker toward its aligned source edge segment, stopping at the segment; recolor the original marker cell to 4. Map the marker's offset along the source segment to the corresponding position on the opposite segment and draw a full perpendicular track of the marker color across the field. Preserve existing segment cells, but include blank cells on the far edge when the mapped track reaches them. Apply the same rule in the rotated orientation for left/right segments. Preserve all unrelated background cells. A key correction from two failed attempts: source rays point toward the aligned source segment, and mapped tracks extend through to the opposite outer edge, including its previously blank cells.",

Align corresponding cells and output a grid the size of either panel: write 2 iff both aligned cells are nonzero; otherwise write 0. Thus zeros in either panel mask the output, and every nonzero lower-panel color maps to 2. The panels and divider may use different colors across instances. Caution: do not output only lower-panel nonzero cells or invert the lower condition; the upper panel also gates every output cell. Preserve alignment and panel dimensions.",
